errors.quote: Since $T_0,S_0$ are bijections agreeing off $\mathcal B$, $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.
errors.problem: As written, the inference does not hold. Two bijections that agree off $\mathcal B$ only make $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fix $S_0(\mathcal B^c)$, which need not equal $\mathcal B^c$. The paper first notes that $T_0$ preserves all guard values, hence $T_0(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B$. That gives $S_0(\mathcal B^c)=T_0(\mathcal B^c)=\mathcal B^c$ and $S_0(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B$.

errors.quote: Each line is, for all segments together, one cyclic shift (sign $\varepsilon$, tested parity $b$) $$y\leftarrow y+\varepsilon\sum_{i=0}^{f-2}2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b]\pmod{2^L}$$
errors.problem: Four of the eight lines update $w$, that is chunk $z$, not $y$. For those lines the paper says to interchange $y$ and $z$ in the formula. As written, every line shifts $y$.

In the paper, $p$ is the parameter of the fixed asymptotic family ($p\to\infty$). In the application it is the working precision $p=6\lceil\log_2n\rceil$, not an address length. The hypothesis $A=O(p)$ only bounds $A$ by $p$. The related phrase 'addresses have $A=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bits' is also loose: record addresses need $\lceil\log_2M\rceil\le A$ bits, and $A_{\rm rect}$ is a bit-length bound.
